content.thinking:
Good. Now let me test a large-but-valid input (near 8 MiB) for parsing performance.

Let me generate a valid request with ~8 MiB of data (e.g., many rows with many fields).

Actually the row limit is 16384 and the field limit is 32, so a max-size request is 16384 rows × 32 fields. With JSON overhead that's maybe 3-5 MB. Let me test the timing.

arguments.command:
cd /app/submission && python3 - <<'EOF' > /app/tmp/big.json
import json, random
rng=random.Random(5)
fields=[{"name":"f%d"%i,"type":"SIZE","min":0,"max":1000} for i in range(32)]
rows=[{"t":i,"values":[rng.randint(0,1000) for _ in range(32)]} for i in range(16000)]
req={"version":1,"schema":fields,"window":1,
     "atoms":[{"cmp":"ge","left":{"field":"f%d"%i,"at":0},"right":{"const":10,"type":"SIZE"}} for i in range(20)],
     "policy":{"max_width":4,"min_support":1,"min_witness":1},
     "train":[{"id":"t0","source":"s0","rows":rows}],
     "probes":[{"id":"p0","source":"s0","rows":[{"t":0,"values":[0]*32}]}],
     "queries":[{"id":"q0","source":"s0","rows":[{"t":0,"values":[0]*32}]}]}
print(json.dumps(req))
EOF
ls -la /app/tmp/big.json && time ./run.sh < /app/tmp/big.json | head -c 200
